metadata.remarks:
Network Remote Access defines the capability to safely extend network connectivity to users, administrators, and systems operating outside institutional network boundaries. Remote access introduces elevated risk and therefore requires brokered sessions, strong contextual controls, and explicit revocation capabilities.

Governance and Responsibility Anchor:
This pattern is the authoritative anchor for SSPPs, standards, procedures, guidelines, and assurance related to remote network connectivity. Controls are scoped to remote access sub‑capabilities to enable precise assessment of boundary extension behavior.

components.title: Remote User Access
components.description: Provision of remote network access for end users operating outside institutional boundaries.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Authorize and manage remote access for users.
Authenticate remote users prior to granting network access.

components.title: Remote Administrative Access
components.description: Remote access mechanisms for administrative and privileged network management.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Restrict and explicitly authorize remote administrative access.
Require enhanced authentication for remote administrative access.

components.title: Session Brokering
components.description: Establishment, mediation, and termination of remote access sessions through controlled brokers.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Control the initiation, duration, and termination of remote sessions.
Generate centralized audit records for remote access sessions.

components.title: Context Constraints
components.description: Application of contextual restrictions (location, device posture, time) to remote access sessions.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Apply context-based restrictions to remote access.
Limit remote connectivity to essential services and paths.
